publications.title: Machine learning for lattice QCD
publications.summary: Machine learning (ML) methods have been explored as a means of optimizing lattice field theory calculations, with increasing interest in recent years. This chapter gives an introduction and summary to the use of ML methods to optimize lattice field theory without introducing any uncontrolled approximations. We focus on those directions which are clearly established as of late 2025, marking the 50th anniversary of the beginning of the study of lattice gauge theory. This chapter is a contribution to the online book ``Lattice QCD at 50 years,'' (LQCD@50), edited by Tanmoy Bhattacharya, Maarten Golterman, Rajan Gupta, Laurent Lellouch, and Steve Sharpe.

publications.title: Primitive Quantum Gates for an $SU(3)$ Discrete Subgroup: $Σ(216\times3)$
publications.summary: We construct a primitive gate set for the digital quantum simulation of the $648$-element discrete subgroup of $SU(3)$, $\dsb$. The five algorithmic primitives are the inversion, group multiplication, trace, group Fourier transform, and kinetic-phase gates, for which we provide qubit and qutrit--qubit decompositions. For a fiducial shear-viscosity calculation on a $10^3$ spatial lattice with $50$ time steps and a total synthesis-error budget of $10^{-8}$, the estimated fault-tolerant costs are $2.3$--$6.8\times10^{10}$ $T$ gates in the qubit architecture and $1.3$--$5.9\times10^{12}$ $R$ gates in the qutrit--qubit architecture.

publications.title: Quark-mass dependence of two-nucleon scattering
publications.summary: Understanding how the properties of the visible Universe depend on the parameters of the Standard Model of particle physics requires \emph{ab initio} theoretical computations. To that end, we investigate the quark-mass dependence of low-energy nucleon-nucleon scattering in the deuteron and dineutron channels. We perform lattice-QCD calculations at pion masses $M_π\approx 200$ and $280$ MeV and compare their results to phenomenology at the physical point and to a previous calculation at $M_π\approx 710$ MeV. Scattering amplitudes, phase shifts, and threshold parameters are determined from finite-volume spectra using quantization conditions that explicitly incorporate long-distance effects from one-pion exchange. We analyze the pion-mass dependence of scattering lengths and effective ranges using chiral effective field theory with Weinberg and Kaplan-Savage-Wise power countings. From this, we estimate the pion-mass derivatives of the inverse scattering lengths and binding momentum, at the physical point. Both power countings indicate that the deuteron unbinds near $M_π\approx 220$ MeV.

publications.title: Quantum Simulation of Hadronization: From String Breaking to Event Generation
publications.summary: High-energy collisions produce large numbers of quarks and gluons that are bound into hadrons by the confining interactions of quantum chromodynamics (QCD). This hadronization process is intrinsically real-time and non-perturbative. Event generators describe hadronization using phenomenological models with parameters fitted to data rather than calculated from QCD. Uncertainties in these models limit the precision of certain measurements at the Large Hadron Collider. Quantum computers could enable first-principles simulations of these dynamics. Existing quantum simulations of gauge theories have demonstrated string-breaking dynamics. This white paper summarizes the conclusions of the InQubator for Quantum Simulation workshop \textit{From String Dynamics to Event Generation with Quantum Simulation}. We develop a roadmap for extending these simulations to inform phenomenological models of hadronization. A sequence of toy models is proposed for connecting current quantum simulations to QCD. The observables that should be extracted are listed, and the challenges that separate present simulations from quantitative predictions are identified. We propose a staged program in which quantum simulations first provide qualitative modifications to event generators and later provide quantitative input.

publications.title: Meson spectroscopy from lattice QCD
publications.summary: Determining the meson spectrum directly from Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) remains a central challenge, since QCD is strongly coupled at low energies and most excited states appear as resonances in hadronic decay channels. Advances in lattice QCD and scattering theory now provide a systematic framework for extracting meson spectra and resonance properties from first principles. Here I present an overview of this program and review current state-of-the-art calculations in meson spectroscopy from lattice QCD. I highlight recent progress in the extraction of resonant and coupled-channel amplitudes, along with frontier developments in three-body dynamics and the determination of meson photo-couplings. Together, these advances are bringing us closer to a comprehensive first-principles description of the excited meson spectrum.
